answer: Sybil defence here rests on a locked stake per identity plus a vault that cannot be replayed: each agent posts its own bond at registration, and a clone funded from the same source is refused at attestation because its vault key must be fresh and unforgeable. Every attestation must also carry a distinct falcon signature chain, so duplicated proofs collapse into one account. A jetty of many fake identities is therefore expensive: the attacker pays one real bond and one long-lived signing chain per voice, while an honest agent pays once, making honest participation cheaper than flooding.
